A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PolyCom research. All 22 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2, including proofs, appendices, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original dense and MoE language-model training, downstream evaluations, activation ablations, and representation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds model-size scaling, longer dense-model training, and ResNet50 experiments on ImageNet-1K.

M1.justification: The PolyCom composition rules, PolyReLU and PolyNorm equations, default third order, coefficient initialization, and FFN integration are retained. Appendix D newly supplies implementation code and checkpointing details without establishing a revision to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Appendix H adds ImageNet-1K image classification, extending actual evaluation beyond language modeling to vision. The original language-training datasets and downstream task coverage remain.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain their baseline membership: SwiGLU, GELU, and ReLU in Table 1; SwiGLU in Tables 2–3; and ReLU/ReLU2 in the variant ablation. New experiments and cost analyses reuse existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds 110M/226M/502M configurations trained on 200B tokens with 2048-token contexts, additional 400B-token dense-model runs, and a 200-epoch ResNet50 evaluation using top-1/top-5 accuracy. These supplement the retained original comparisons. Table 7 reports a dense minimum learning rate of 3e-5, conflicting with 1.5e-5 in both versions' Section 4.1; this does not establish that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds model-size sensitivity analysis across 110M–1.3B parameters. Appendix F adds analytical FLOP and memory comparisons with and without checkpointing. The original order, composition, ReLU-variant, weight-rank, and layer-similarity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed choices, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The added experiments retain point estimates and curves without quantified uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the original plots retain their results. New Figures 8 and 13 report scaling and 400B-token results favoring PolyCom. Appendix H reports PolyNorm top-1/top-5 accuracy of 75.117%/92.099%, exceeding ReLU by 0.204/0.068 percentage points. Tables 8–9 add numerical cost estimates. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Theorem 2 narrows its lower-bound statement to the existence of hard PolyReLU networks, and Lemma 2 explicitly fixes the polynomial order. Appendix B formalizes the previously cited optimality lower bound and its parameter-count implication. The principal approximation rates and existing proofs remain; Lemma 1's proof is relocated.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about PolyCom, optimal approximation rates, and improved LLM accuracy and convergence. Added experiments support these claims without redefining the stated main contributions.

C2.justification: The general expressivity-equivalence assertion is removed; Section 3 instead interprets PolyNorm as at least as expressive as PolyReLU. New discussion connects stability to normalization and clipping, warns about PolyReLU in non-transformer architectures, recommends PolyNorm there, and qualifies computational overhead through checkpointing.

D1.justification: Appendix D supplies PyTorch implementations, while Table 7 newly documents warmup, weight decay, clipping, initialization, and MoE loss coefficients. Additional configuration and checkpointing details improve reproducibility; the code-access link is retained. However, Algorithm 2 uses RMS-style normalization with epsilon, whereas the unchanged Equation 3 specifies L2 normalization, leaving a documentation inconsistency.

R1.justification: Section 5 newly acknowledges Li et al. (2019), stating that rectified power units achieve the same approximation rate as PolyReLU. Additional references cover activation research, transformer applications, and the vision experiment. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose remain. v2 makes localized language corrections, updates publication and author-note formatting, adds acknowledgments, moves Lemma 1's proof into Appendix A, and organizes added material into dedicated appendix sections.

P2.justification: v2 adds scaling, vision, and longer-training plots; Tables 7–10; and two implementation listings. It also expands the activation-definition table and rearranges existing displays. The original appendix Figures 8–11 survive as Figures 10–12 and 14, rather than being removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves practical assessment through scaling, longer-training and vision evidence, explicit cost estimates, and substantially better implementation documentation. The corrected lower-bound quantifier and acknowledgment of prior matching approximation rates also improve precision. These benefits are tempered by absent experimental uncertainty and new documentation conflicts concerning the learning-rate minimum and RMS versus L2 normalization. The additions strengthen the paper, while leaving the central empirical findings unchanged.
